Conclusion Completion of re-immunisation schedules post-HSCT is suboptimal, leaving gaps in protection against vaccine-preventable infections. There is considerable delay between clearance for re-immunisation and commencement. Uptake of MCV and the practice of confirming seroconversion is highly variable.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on gaps in protection against measles virus and related vaccine-preventable infections in patients post-haematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) for primary immunodeficiency (PID) syndromes. The study analyzed HSCTs conducted at Starship Children's Hospital in New Zealand between 2018 and 2025, focusing on children aged ≤18 years. The review highlights that re-immunisation schedules post-HSCT are suboptimal, with delays in vaccine commencement and variability in measles-containing vaccine (MCV) uptake. Only 9% of patients were fully up-to-date with re-immunisations, and 40% had post-MCV measles serology checked, with one individual remaining seronegative despite two doses. These findings underscore the need for improved adherence to vaccination protocols and further research on vaccine effectiveness in this vulnerable population.

abstract_zh: 简介:原发性免疫缺陷 (PID) 综合征患者在造血干细胞移植 (HSCT) 后容易受到 疫苗 可预防的感染。免疫重建后及时重新免疫至关重要。方法:通过机构数据库确定 2018-2025 年在新西兰 Starship 儿童医院进行的用于治疗儿童(年龄≤18 岁)的 HSCT。审查了当地和国家电子病历、临床和实验室数据以及 疫苗接种 记录(新西兰免疫登记册)。HSCT 后再免疫资格标准和审核标准基于新西兰国家儿童癌症网络指南。结果:在接受 236 次 HSCT 的 197 名独特患者中,28 名患者因 PID 而接受 HSCT。如果患者目前因临床原因未清除重新免疫 (n = 2) 或在 HSCT 6 个月内死亡 (n = 4),则患者被排除。本初步报告纳入了 22 名符合重新免疫资格的患者。22 人中的 1 人 (4.5%) 尚未开始重新免疫。重新免疫许可日期和第一个非活体 疫苗 给药之间的中位时间为 64 天(四分位距 [IQR] 9-126 天)。33% 的患者 (7/21) 出现与标准 疫苗接种 序列的偏差。在任何一次访问中,85% (18/21) 的人没有获得所有符合条件的 疫苗。9% (2/22) 在审核时完全了解最新的重新免疫情况。20 名患者有资格接受实时 疫苗 治疗。65% (13/20) 接受了至少一剂含有 麻疹 的 疫苗 (MCV)。最后一次血液制品给药与首次注射 MCV 之间的中位时间为 669 天(IQR 476-766 天)。50% (10/20) 接受了 2 剂 MCV。40% (4/10) 进行了 MCV 后 麻疹 血清学 检查;尽管注射了 2 剂 MCV,但仍有一名患者血清呈阴性。结论:HSCT 后重新免疫计划的完成情况并不理想,在针对 疫苗 可预防感染的保护方面存在差距。重新免疫许可和开始之间存在相当大的延迟。MCV 的摄取和确认血清转化的做法差异很大。

title: Prevalence of diarrhea and its determinants among children under five years of age in rural Kebeles of East Gurage Zone, central Ethiopia: A cross-sectional study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Diarrheal disease remains a major cause of death among children under five, particularly in resource-limited settings. Despite the availability of effective water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions, the burden of diarrhea remains high in Ethiopia. This study aims to assess the prevalence of diarrhea and its associated factors among under-five children in East Gurage Zone, central Ethiopia. METHODOLOGY: This baseline survey was part of a four-arm cluster randomized trial (cRCT). Using the Hayes and Bennett formula, we set the sample size at 840 participants (210 per arm) with 95% confidence and 80% power. Data were cleaned in Epi Data 3.1 and analyzed in SPSS 25. Reliability testing showed weak internal consistency, with Cronbach's alpha of 0.36 for knowledge, 0.46 for practice, and 0.40 for wealth, reflecting few items and distinct domains. Childhood diarrhea associated factors were examined using bivariate and multivariate Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) models, accounting for clustering, with significance set at p < 0.05 and 95% CI. RESULTS: Diarrhea prevalence was high in the study area (25.7%) (95% CI: 22.8-28.7). Maternal age 24-34 (AOR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.27-0.53), hand washing at critical times (AOR = 0.20, 95% CI: 0.07-0.58), both soap and water use (AOR = 0.09, 95% CI: 0.03-0.33), using tightly covered (AOR = 0.17, 95% CI: 0.03-0.91) and clean water containers (AOR = 0.47, 95% CI: 0.26-0.84), measles vaccination (AOR = 0.07, 95% CI: 0.04-0.13), fetching water <30 minutes round-trip (AOR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.12-0.57), and latrine availability (AOR = 0.28, 95% CI: 0.19-0.43) were significantly associated with lower odds of under-five diarrhea. CONCLUSION: Diarrhea affected one in four children (25.7%; 95% CI: 22.8-28.7), indicating a substantial burden in the study area, particularly in rural communities. Strengthening WASH interventions and fostering coordinated efforts among government, local authorities, and development partners is essential to reduce this burden. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07158632.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study aimed to assess the prevalence of diarrhea and its associated factors among under-five children in rural Kebeles of East Gurage Zone, central Ethiopia. The study was part of a four-arm cluster randomized trial with a sample size of 840 participants. Data were analyzed using SPSS 25, and reliability testing showed weak internal consistency for knowledge, practice, and wealth domains. Diarrhea prevalence was found to be high at 25.7% (95% CI: 22.8-28.7). Factors significantly associated with lower odds of under-five diarrhea included maternal age 24-34, hand washing at critical times, both soap and water use, using tightly covered and clean water containers, measles vaccination, fetching water <30 minutes round-trip, and latrine availability. The authors concluded that strengthening WASH interventions and fostering coordinated efforts among government, local authorities, and development partners is essential to reduce the burden of diarrhea. The study's findings are limited by the weak internal consistency of the reliability testing, and the evidence is moderate in strength.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项基线调查是四组整群随机试验 (cRCT) 的一部分。使用 Hayes 和 Bennett 公式,我们将样本量设置为 840 名参与者(每组 210 名),置信度为 95%,功效为 80%。
elements_zh.methods: 数据在 Epi Data 3.1 中进行清理,并在 SPSS 25 中进行分析。使用双变量和多变量广义估计方程 (GEE) 模型检查儿童腹泻相关因素,考虑聚类,显着性设置为 p < 0.05 和 95% CI。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究区域的腹泻 患病率 较高 (25.7%) (95% CI: 22.8-28.7)。可靠性测试显示内部一致性较弱,知识的克伦巴赫阿尔法为0.36,实践的克朗巴赫阿尔法为0.46,财富的克朗巴赫阿尔法为0.40,反映的项目较少且领域不同。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: Maternal age 24-34 (AOR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.27-0.53), hand washing at critical times (AOR = 0.20, 95% CI: 0.07-0.58), both soap and water use (AOR = 0.09, 95% CI: 0.03-0.33), using tightly covered and clean water containers (AOR = 0.17, 95% CI: 0.03-0.91), measles vaccination (AOR = 0.07, 95% CI: 0.04-0.13), fetching water <30 minutes round-trip (AOR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.12-0.57), and latrine availability (AOR = 0.28, 95% CI: 0.19-0.43) were significantly associated with lower odds of under-five diarrhea.
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 四分之一的儿童患有腹泻(25.7%;95% CI:22.8-28.7),这表明研究地区,特别是农村社区,承受着巨大的负担。加强 WASH 干预措施并促进政府、地方当局和发展伙伴之间的协调努力对于减轻这一负担至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告与 麻疹病毒 相关的具体限制。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 腹泻病仍然是五岁以下儿童死亡的主要原因,特别是在资源有限的环境中。尽管提供了有效的水、环境卫生和个人卫生 (WASH) 干预措施,但埃塞俄比亚的腹泻负担仍然很高。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项基线调查是四组整群随机试验 (cRCT) 的一部分。使用 Hayes 和 Bennett 公式,我们将样本量设置为 840 名参与者(每组 210 名),置信度为 95%,功效为 80%。
analysis_zh.methods: 数据在 Epi Data 3.1 中进行清理,并在 SPSS 25 中进行分析。使用双变量和多变量广义估计方程 (GEE) 模型检查儿童腹泻相关因素,考虑聚类,显着性设置为 p < 0.05 和 95% CI。
analysis_zh.main_results: 研究区域的腹泻 患病率 较高 (25.7%) (95% CI: 22.8-28.7)。可靠性测试显示内部一致性较弱,知识的克伦巴赫阿尔法为0.36,实践的克朗巴赫阿尔法为0.46,财富的克朗巴赫阿尔法为0.40,反映的项目较少且领域不同。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 四分之一的儿童患有腹泻(25.7%;95% CI:22.8-28.7),这表明研究地区,特别是农村社区,承受着巨大的负担。加强 WASH 干预措施并促进政府、地方当局和发展伙伴之间的协调努力对于减轻这一负担至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告与 麻疹病毒 相关的具体限制。

title: Incidence of Infectious Diseases in Bulgaria over a 50-Year Period (1974–2023)
abstract: Objective: To investigate the long-term trends and dynamics of acute infectious diseases morbidity in Bulgaria across half of century of significant socio-economic transitions, healthcare reforms, and geopolitical integrations. Methods: retrospective epidemiological study was conducted covering a 50-year period (1974–2023). Aggregated data from 10 consecutive five-year cohorts were extracted from official statutory reporting networks managed by the National Statistical Institute (NSI), the National Center for Public Health and Analyses (NCPHA), and the National Center for Infectious and Parasitic Diseases (NCIPD). Results: Drastic shifts in infectious disease dynamics correlate directly with national immunization strategies, economic transitions, and the entry into force of healthcare reforms. Mass immunoprophylaxis achieved successful elimination patterns or historic minimums for core respiratory and neuro-invasive pathogens, including diphtheria and rubella. However, recent 2020-2023 metrics reveal sub-optimal measles-mumpsrubella (MMR) and pertussis coverage, sparking a notable upward trend in pertussis morbidity and infant mortality. Pathogens lacking mass vaccination frameworks, such as varicella and scarlet fever, exhibited sharp post-pandemic resurgences following the relaxation of containment measures. Climate-driven shifts are expanding vector-borne footprints, such as West Nile fever. Furthermore, the COVID-19 pandemic introduced substantial diagnostic reporting artefacts and a heavy excess mortality burden. Conclusions: Long-term surveillance data confirms a persistent overall decline in vaccine-preventable diseases alongside expanding relative shares of intestinal, emerging vector-borne, and non-vaccine-preventable respiratory infections. Tracking these dynamics provides a vital public health baseline for mitigating vaccine hesitancy and changing ecological disease boundaries.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 调查保加利亚半个世纪以来重大社会经济转型、医疗改革和地缘政治一体化期间急性传染病发病率的长期趋势和动态。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 进行了一项涵盖 50 年(1974 年至 2023 年)的回顾性流行病学研究。
elements_zh.methods: 连续 10 个五年期 队列研究 的汇总数据取自国家统计研究所 (NSI)、国家公共卫生和分析中心 (NCPHA) 以及国家传染病和寄生虫病中心 (NCIPD) 管理的官方法定报告网络。
elements_zh.main_results: 传染病动态的急剧变化与国家免疫战略、经济转型和医疗改革的生效直接相关。大规模免疫预防成功地消除了核心呼吸道和神经侵袭性病原体(包括白喉和风疹)或达到历史最低水平。然而,最近的 2020-2023 年指标显示,麻疹-流行性腮腺炎风疹 (MMR) 和百日咳覆盖率并非最佳,引发了百日咳发病率和婴儿 死亡率 的显着上升趋势。气候驱动的变化正在扩大 媒介 传播的足迹,例如西尼罗河热。此外,COVID-19 大流行带来了大量的诊断报告假象和沉重的超额 死亡率 负担。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释了这些发现,指出大规模免疫预防在实现核心呼吸道和神经侵袭性病原体消除模式方面取得的成功,但也强调了最近对 MMR 和百日咳的次优覆盖,这导致了百日咳发病率和婴儿 死亡率 的上升趋势。他们还注意到 媒介 传播的足迹不断扩大,以及 COVID-19 大流行对诊断报告和 死亡率 的影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 长期 监测 数据证实,疫苗 可预防疾病的总体持续下降,同时肠道、新出现的 媒介 传播的疾病和非 疫苗 可预防的呼吸道感染的相对比例不断扩大。跟踪这些动态为减轻 疫苗 犹豫和改变生态疾病边界提供了重要的公共卫生基线。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到数据的回顾性以及 COVID-19 大流行带来的诊断假象的可能性的限制。证据强度中等。

abstract_zh: 目的:调查保加利亚半个世纪重大社会经济转型、医疗改革和地缘政治一体化期间急性传染病发病率的长期趋势和动态。方法:进行为期50年(1974年至2023年)的回顾性流行病学研究。连续 10 个五年期 队列研究 的汇总数据取自国家统计研究所 (NSI)、国家公共卫生和分析中心 (NCPHA) 以及国家传染病和寄生虫病中心 (NCIPD) 管理的官方法定报告网络。结果:传染病动态的巨大变化与国家免疫战略、经济转型和医疗改革的生效直接相关。大规模免疫预防成功地消除了核心呼吸道和神经侵袭性病原体(包括白喉和风疹)或达到历史最低水平。然而,最近的 2020-2023 年指标显示,麻疹-流行性腮腺炎风疹 (MMR) 和百日咳覆盖率并非最佳,引发了百日咳发病率和婴儿 死亡率 的显着上升趋势。缺乏大规模 疫苗接种 框架的病原体,如水痘和猩红热,在遏制措施放松后表现出大流行后的急剧复苏。气候驱动的变化正在扩大 媒介 传播的足迹,例如西尼罗河热。此外,COVID-19 大流行带来了大量的诊断报告假象和沉重的超额 死亡率 负担。结论:长期 疫苗 数据证实,疫苗 可预防疾病总体持续下降,同时肠道、新出现的 媒介 传播疾病和非 疫苗 可预防呼吸道感染的相对比例有所扩大。跟踪这些动态为减轻 疫苗 犹豫和改变生态疾病边界提供了重要的公共卫生基线。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释了这些发现,指出大规模免疫预防在实现核心呼吸道和神经侵袭性病原体消除模式方面取得的成功,但也强调了最近对 MMR 和百日咳的次优覆盖,这导致了百日咳发病率和婴儿 死亡率 的上升趋势。他们还注意到 媒介 传播的足迹不断扩大,以及 COVID-19 大流行对诊断报告和 死亡率 的影响。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 长期 监测 数据证实,疫苗 可预防疾病的总体持续下降,同时肠道、新出现的 媒介 传播的疾病和非 疫苗 可预防的呼吸道感染的相对比例不断扩大。跟踪这些动态为减轻 疫苗 犹豫和改变生态疾病边界提供了重要的公共卫生基线。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到数据的回顾性以及 COVID-19 大流行带来的诊断假象的可能性的限制。证据强度中等。

title: Viral Pathogens as Global Health Threats: Review of Transmissibility, Lethality, and Pandemic Potential
abstract: Viral pathogens vary substantially in their transmissibility, lethality, and potential to cause widespread epidemics or pandemics. Measles, for example, is exceptionally contagious but has relatively low case fatality in populations with access to modern medical care. Conversely, rabies, Nipah virus, Ebola virus, and Marburg virus can cause severe disease with high case fatality rates but generally exhibit limited sustained human-to-human transmission. The greatest global threats, therefore, are not necessarily the most contagious or lethal viruses, but those that combine efficient transmission, substantial clinical severity, zoonotic reservoirs, evolutionary adaptability, and limited preventive or therapeutic options. The COVID-19 pandemic illustrated this convergence of risk factors, demonstrating how efficient transmission, including presymptomatic and asymptomatic spread, coupled with clinically significant disease can produce devastating global consequences. Influenza A viruses remain a major pandemic concern because of their extensive animal reservoirs, capacity for antigenic evolution, and established history of human pandemics. Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) is particularly concerning given the high case fatality observed among confirmed human cases, although sustained human-to-human transmission has not been established. In contrast, henipaviruses and filoviruses pose substantial clinical threats because of their high lethality, despite comparatively limited transmissibility. This review critically examines major viral threats through three interconnected determinants of global health risk: transmissibility, infection fatality risk, and the biological and epidemiological factors governing their epidemic and pandemic potential.
journal: Advances in Social Sciences Research Journal

title_zh: 病毒病原体作为全球健康威胁:传播性、致死性和大流行潜力的回顾
source_body_en: Viral pathogens vary substantially in their transmissibility, lethality, and potential to cause widespread epidemics or pandemics. Measles, for example, is exceptionally contagious but has relatively low case fatality in populations with access to modern medical care. Conversely, rabies, Nipah virus, Ebola virus, and Marburg virus can cause severe disease with high case fatality rates but generally exhibit limited sustained human-to-human transmission. The greatest global threats, therefore, are not necessarily the most contagious or lethal viruses, but those that combine efficient transmission, substantial clinical severity, zoonotic reservoirs, evolutionary adaptability, and limited preventive or therapeutic options. The COVID-19 pandemic illustrated this convergence of risk factors, demonstrating how efficient transmission, including presymptomatic and asymptomatic spread, coupled with clinically significant disease can produce devastating global consequences. Influenza A viruses remain a major pandemic concern because of their extensive animal reservoirs, capacity for antigenic evolution, and established history of human pandemics. Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) is particularly concerning given the high case fatality observed among confirmed human cases, although sustained human-to-human transmission has not been established. In contrast, henipaviruses and filoviruses pose substantial clinical threats because of their high lethality, despite comparatively limited transmissibility. This review critically examines major viral threats through three interconnected determinants of global health risk: transmissibility, infection fatality risk, and the biological and epidemiological factors governing their epidemic and pandemic potential.

title: An Ancient p53–miR-128 Axis Restricts Mucosal and Placental Viral Entry by Suppressing Nectin-4
abstract: Host cell-surface receptors dictate viral tropism, tissue entry, and cross-barrier transmission. Although Nectin-4 (encoded by PVRL4) has recently been established as the essential epithelial receptor for major respiratory and teratogenic pathogens—including Measles virus and Rubella virus—the endogenous host mechanisms governing its expression remain poorly defined. Because physical wet-lab experimentation is absent in this study, we utilize advanced computational systems-biology modeling, network integration, and predictive multi-omics simulations. Here, we uncover an evolutionarily conserved host restriction pathway wherein the ancient antiviral guardian p53 coordinates with the longevity factor FOXO3a to deploy microRNA-128 (miR-128), which post-transcriptionally silences PVRL4. Systematic in silico evaluation of public expression repositories (GEO/Harmonizome) reveals a robust inverse correlation between p53 pathway activation states and PVRL4 surface density across polarized airway epithelia. By modeling the repression of surface Nectin-4 density, this predictive axis blocks the receptor-mediated membrane fusion required by Nectin-4-tropic viruses. These computational findings position the p53–FOXO3a–miR-128–Nectin-4 axis as a vital mucosal defense mechanism, demonstrating how ancient host restriction networks target specialized viral entry portals.

abstract_zh: 宿主 细胞表面受体决定病毒趋向性、组织进入和跨屏障 传播。尽管 Nectin-4(由 PVRL4 编码)最近已被确定为主要呼吸道和致畸病原体(包括 麻疹病毒 和风疹病毒)的重要上皮受体,但控制其表达的内源性 麻疹病毒 机制仍不清楚。由于本研究中没有物理湿实验室实验,因此我们利用先进的计算系统-生物学建模、网络集成和预测性多组学模拟。在这里,我们发现了一条进化上保守的 宿主 限制途径,其中古老的 抗病毒药物 守护者 p53 与长寿因子 FOXO3a 协调部署 microRNA-128 (miR-128),从而在转录后沉默 PVRL4。对公共表达库 (GEO/Harmonizome) 的系统计算机评估揭示了 p53 通路激活状态与极化气道上皮的 PVRL4 表面密度之间存在强大的负相关性。通过模拟表面 Nectin-4 密度的抑制,该预测轴阻断了 Nectin-4-tropic 病毒所需的受体介导的膜融合。这些计算结果将 p53–FOXO3a–miR-128–Nectin-4 轴定位为重要的粘膜防御机制,展示了古老的 宿主 限制网络如何针对专门的病毒进入门户。

title: Climatic variability and routine childhood vaccine uptake in high-risk urban settlements of Karachi, Pakistan: a longitudinal fixed-effects panel analysis
abstract: Climate variability may disrupt routine immunization in rapidly growing cities, where informal settlements combine high climatic exposure with fragile health services, yet longitudinal urban evidence from low- and middle-income countries is limited. We examined associations between monthly climatic conditions and routine childhood vaccine doses in 14 public and private health facilities serving nine high-risk urban union councils of Karachi, Pakistan, using 266 facility-month observations (June 2023–December 2024). Monthly doses of Bacille Calmette–Guérin (BCG), pentavalent (Penta-1 to Penta-3), inactivated poliovirus (IPV-1) and measles–rubella (MR-1) vaccines were linked with reanalysis-based maximum temperature, relative humidity and wind speed, satellite-based rainfall, night-time light (NTL) and catchment population. One-way fixed-effects panel models with facility-clustered standard errors were fitted for each vaccine, with five sensitivity analyses. In the main models, wind speed was negatively associated with doses of all six vaccines (standardized β = −0.150 to −0.491), maximum temperature with five, and relative humidity positively with all six. Rainfall was negatively associated with BCG doses (β = −0.285, p < 0.001) in every specification, whereas its positive associations with Penta-2 and MR-1 did not persist after lagged climatic terms were added. The temperature association persisted only for BCG and Penta-2 when the start-up months were excluded. NTL was associated with the multi-visit doses Penta-2, Penta-3 and IPV-1. Climatic associations with routine immunization in urban informal settings therefore differ by vaccine, supporting vaccine-specific, climate-informed urban immunization planning.

title: Overview of Health Status among Roma Population in Romania: A Scoping Review
abstract: Background: Roma are widely recognized as Europe ‘s largest ethnic minority and in-dependent estimates suggest that up to two million people live in Romania. Despite well-documented socioeconomic disadvantage, no prior review has synthesized evi-dence on the health status of Roma in Romania. Objectives: This scoping review mapped the literature on healthcare access, quality of life, chronic disease burden and communicable disease exposure among Roma communities in Romania. Methods: Us-ing the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we con-ducted a systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Science Direct and supplemented by grey literature and reference-list screening, for studies published 2010–2025 in English or Romanian. Results: Thirty-nine sources (35 studies and 4 in-stitutional reports) met the inclusion criteria. Roma communities experience a life-expectancy gap of 3.5–4.6 years, markedly lower preventive-care uptake (39% vs 71% in the general population), and high rates of being uninsured (42–59%). Chronic disease burden was substantially higher than in the general population: hypertension prevalence ranged 33–67%, type 2 diabetes from 10–29%, and obesity from 32–62%, with evidence of earlier onset and more severe complications, including higher pro-gression to chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease. Health-related quality of life and mental health indicators were uniformly worse among Roma. Evidence on communicable diseases was sparse but suggested elevated hepatitis B/C prevalence and greater severity of measles and COVID-19. Conclusions: Roma communities in Romania experience markedly poorer health outcomes across nearly all domains ex-amined, driven by intersecting socioeconomic, structural and behavioral determinants.

title: A decade of infectious disease trends in Northern Cyprus, 2014–2024
abstract: Background Longitudinal infectious-disease surveillance is difficult to interpret when case definitions, diagnostic practices, and reporting structures change over time. Northern Cyprus remains underrepresented in multi-disease surveillance literature. We therefore reconstructed and harmonized official notifiable-disease data to characterize major temporal patterns while preserving epidemiologic comparability. Methods A retrospective ecological time-series analysis was conducted using official Ministry of Health surveillance records for major notifiable infections from 2014 to 2025. The primary analytical period was 2014–2024, with 2025 retained descriptively. Disease indicators were harmonized using predefined clinical and epidemiologic rules, while non-equivalent categories were analyzed within separate reporting eras. Official Statistical Institute data were used for independent cross-validation of selected annual totals and for population denominators. Notification rates per 100,000 were calculated for 2019–2024, and formal modeling was restricted to sufficiently stable series. Results Disease patterns were heterogeneous. Several infections remained sparse, whereas measles showed episodic activity with renewed notifications after 2022. Varicella fluctuated substantially, with no significant monotonic trend after adjustment for overdispersion (NRR 0.844, 95% CI 0.664–1.074; p = 0.169). Tuberculosis showed the strongest recent signal, rising from 0.44 per 100,000 in 2022 to 13.42 in 2023 and remaining elevated at 9.32 in 2024. Viral hepatitis and HIV/STI patterns were strongly influenced by surveillance-definition changes. Conclusion Notifiable infections in Northern Cyprus showed distinct temporal patterns, including episodic vaccine-preventable disease activity, continued notification of blood-borne and sexually transmitted infections, and a marked recent tuberculosis signal. To our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive harmonized multi-disease analysis of official surveillance in Northern Cyprus, providing an important epidemiologic baseline for an underrepresented Eastern Mediterranean setting. Stable case definitions, compatible denominators, and stronger laboratory linkage are essential for distinguishing true epidemiologic change from reporting effects and supporting targeted public-health action.

title_zh: 2014-2024 年北塞浦路斯十年传染病趋势
source_body_en: Background Longitudinal infectious-disease surveillance is difficult to interpret when case definitions, diagnostic practices, and reporting structures change over time. Northern Cyprus remains underrepresented in multi-disease surveillance literature. We therefore reconstructed and harmonized official notifiable-disease data to characterize major temporal patterns while preserving epidemiologic comparability. Methods A retrospective ecological time-series analysis was conducted using official Ministry of Health surveillance records for major notifiable infections from 2014 to 2025. The primary analytical period was 2014–2024, with 2025 retained descriptively. Disease indicators were harmonized using predefined clinical and epidemiologic rules, while non-equivalent categories were analyzed within separate reporting eras. Official Statistical Institute data were used for independent cross-validation of selected annual totals and for population denominators. Notification rates per 100,000 were calculated for 2019–2024, and formal modeling was restricted to sufficiently stable series. Results Disease patterns were heterogeneous. Several infections remained sparse, whereas measles showed episodic activity with renewed notifications after 2022. Varicella fluctuated substantially, with no significant monotonic trend after adjustment for overdispersion (NRR 0.844, 95% CI 0.664–1.074; p = 0.169). Tuberculosis showed the strongest recent signal, rising from 0.44 per 100,000 in 2022 to 13.42 in 2023 and remaining elevated at 9.32 in 2024. Viral hepatitis and HIV/STI patterns were strongly influenced by surveillance-definition changes. Conclusion Notifiable infections in Northern Cyprus showed distinct temporal patterns, including episodic vaccine-preventable disease activity, continued notification of blood-borne and sexually transmitted infections, and a marked recent tuberculosis signal. To our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive harmonized multi-disease analysis of official surveillance in Northern Cyprus, providing an important epidemiologic baseline for an underrepresented Eastern Mediterranean setting. Stable case definitions, compatible denominators, and stronger laboratory linkage are essential for distinguishing true epidemiologic change from reporting effects and supporting targeted public-health action.

title: Closing Somalia’s childhood vaccination gap in the digital era: a perspective on misinformation, trust, and access
abstract: Somalia’s childhood immunization coverage has improved, but important gaps remain across vaccine doses, populations, and places. The latest WHO/UNICEF estimates for 2025 report 77% coverage for the first dose of diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis-containing vaccine (DTP1), 72% for DTP3, and 61% for the first measles-containing vaccine (MCV1), while the 2020 Somali Health and Demographic Survey documented far lower household-survey coverage. These measures are not directly interchangeable and illustrate both progress and continuing uncertainty in a fragile data environment. This Perspective argues that misinformation, trust, and access should be examined together, while recognizing that Somalia-specific evidence on digital vaccine misinformation remains limited. Established WHO Behavioural and Social Drivers of vaccination (BeSD) and WHO/UNICEF social-listening guidance are therefore adapted into an operational pathway for Somalia rather than presented as a new behavioral theory. The adaptation specifies responsible actors, offline and digital listening channels, linguistic and data-system requirements, service-linkage rules, safeguards for conflict settings, and an evaluation strategy. A preferred evaluation would use phased matched-district implementation with DTP3 coverage as the primary outcome, complemented by zero-dose, timeliness, missed-opportunity, responsiveness, and equity indicators. Digital listening should be treated as one sentinel input among community and service data, not as a population-representative measure. The public health value of the pathway ultimately depends on whether verified concerns are translated into trusted communication and reachable vaccination services, especially for displaced, nomadic, insecure, and digitally excluded communities.

abstract_zh: 索马里的儿童免疫覆盖率有所提高,但 疫苗 剂量、人群和地点之间仍存在重要差距。世卫组织/联合国儿童基金会对 2025 年的最新估计报告称,首剂含白喉-破伤风-百日咳的 疫苗 (DTP1) 覆盖率为 77%,DTP3 为 72%,首剂含 麻疹 (MCV1) 的覆盖率为 61%,而 2020 年索马里健康和人口调查记录的覆盖率要低得多家庭调查覆盖范围。这些措施不能直接互换,它们说明了脆弱数据环境中的进展和持续的不确定性。本观点认为,错误信息、信任和获取应一起审查,同时认识到索马里有关数字 疫苗 错误信息的具体证据仍然有限。因此,既定的世卫组织 疫苗接种 (BeSD) 行为和社会驱动因素和世卫组织/联合国儿童基金会社会倾听指南被改编为索马里的操作途径,而不是作为新的行为理论提出。该改编规定了负责任的参与者、离线和数字收听渠道、语言和数据系统要求、服务链接规则、冲突设置的保障措施以及评估策略。首选的评估将采用分阶段匹配区实施,以 DTP3 覆盖率作为主要结果,并辅以零剂量、及时性、错失机会、响应性和公平性指标。数字聆听应被视为社区和服务数据中的一个哨兵输入,而不是一种具有人口代表性的措施。该途径的公共卫生价值最终取决于经过验证的担忧是否转化为可信的沟通和可达的 疫苗接种 服务,特别是对于流离失所、游牧、不安全和数字排斥的社区。

title: A RARE CASE OF ACUTE IMMUNE THROMBOCYTOPENIC PURPURA TEMPORALLY ASSOCIATED WITH ROUTINE TWO-MONTH IMMUNIZATION.
abstract: Background: Immune thrombocytopenic purpura is one of the causes of platelet deficiency. Although vaccinations, particularly MMR, have been reported as a potential temporal trigger, ITP following routine infant immunisation is very rare. Case Summary: We describe the case of a previously healthy 2-month-old infant who was brought to the Emergency Department by his parents with complaints of a spreading non-blanching petechial rash and bruising, which started three days back, initially more prominent over the legs and later on spreading towards the chest. The baby was born at full term by spontaneous vaginal delivery requiring vacuum assistance and no bleeding and bruising were observed at the time of delivery and he didn’t require any admission at the time of birth. The baby on presentation was clinically well, was tolerating oral feeds, there was no history of fever, and no history of preceding viral illness; there was also no history of any trauma. Of note, the infant received his routine childhood vaccinations, including 6 in 1, PCV, Men B, and oral rotavirus 15 days ago. The mother also noted bruising and swelling at the Men B injection site. Method: Upon arrival to the ED after a detailed history, blood tests were done, and initial investigations demonstrated isolated severe thrombocytopenia, with a platelet count of 6 × 109/L, hemoglobin of 10.5 g/dL, and white blood cell count of 9.4 × 109/L. Blood film showed thrombocytopenia with no evidence of platelet clumping noted. The initial film showed neutropenia with an absolute neutrophil count of 0.74 x 109/L and occasional reactive lymphocytes. No blast cells were seen. Coagulation studies were also done and were normal. His cranial ultrasonography was also reported as normal. The extended respiratory viral panel was negative, Epstein–Barr virus, and cytomegalovirus testing were negative as well. The patient was then discussed with the paeds hematology team and a diagnosis of acute immune thrombocytopenia was made. Considering the really low platelet count, it was planned to give IVIG (intravenous immunoglobulin), and the infant received one dose of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). The patient remained stable afterward, and repeat FBC (full blood count) showed an improving trend in the platelet count; as the platelet count started to improve, hematology advised discharging him and doing weekly platelet counts. Platelet counts improved to 68 × 109/L two weeks after treatment and subsequently normalised to 508 × 109/L at five months' follow-up. Routine immunisations were temporarily deferred until platelet recovery and were later resumed according to the national immunisation schedule. The family was also reassured that future measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccination was not contraindicated. Conclusion: This case highlights the importance of recognizing ITP in an otherwise well-appearing child who presents with bruising and petechiae with a blood film showing isolated thrombocytopenia. It is also important that we exclude other alternative causes and promptly treat ITP with IVIG after discussion with the hematology team. Also, close haematology follow-up resulted in complete platelet recovery and safe resumption of routine childhood immunisations.

abstract_zh: 背景:免疫性血小板减少性紫癜是血小板缺乏的原因之一。尽管 疫苗接种,特别是 MMR,已被报道为潜在的时间触发因素,但常规婴儿免疫接种后的 ITP 非常罕见。病例摘要:我们描述了一名先前健康的 2 个月大婴儿的病例,他被父母带到急诊室,抱怨三天前开始出现扩散的非变白的点状皮疹和瘀伤,最初在腿部更加突出,后来向胸部蔓延。婴儿足月出生,通过自然阴道分娩,需要真空辅助,分娩时没有观察到出血和瘀伤,出生时不需要任何入院。就诊的婴儿临床表现良好,能够耐受经口喂养,没有发烧史,也没有既往病毒性疾病史;也没有任何外伤史。值得注意的是,该婴儿于 15 天前接受了童年常规 疫苗接种,包括 6 合 1、PCV、Men B 和口服轮状病毒。这位母亲还注意到 Men B 注射部位有瘀伤和肿胀。方法:在详细询问病史后到达急诊室后,进行了血液检查,初步检查显示孤立性严重血小板减少症,血小板计数为 6 × 109/L,血红蛋白为 10.5 g/dL,白细胞计数为 9.4 × 109/L。血涂片显示血小板减少,没有发现血小板聚集的证据。最初的胶片显示中性粒细胞减少症,中性粒细胞绝对计数为 0.74 x 109/L,偶尔有反应性淋巴细胞。没有看到母细胞。还进行了凝血研究,结果正常。他的颅骨超声检查也报告为正常。扩展呼吸道病毒检测结果呈阴性,爱泼斯坦-巴尔病毒和巨细胞病毒检测也呈阴性。随后与 paeds 血液学团队对该患者进行了讨论,并制定了急性免疫性血小板减少症的 诊断。考虑到血小板计数确实较低,计划给予IVIG(静脉注射免疫球蛋白),婴儿接受了一剂静脉注射免疫球蛋白(IVIG)。此后患者病情稳定,复查FBC(全血细胞计数)显示血小板计数有改善趋势;随着血小板计数开始改善,血液学建议他出院并每周进行血小板计数。治疗 两周后血小板计数改善至 68 × 109/L,随后在五个月的随访中正常化至 508 × 109/L。常规免疫接种暂时推迟至血小板恢复后,随后根据国家免疫接种计划恢复。家人也放心,未来的 麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹 (MMR) 疫苗接种 没有禁忌症。结论:该病例强调了识别 ITP 的重要性,该儿童在其他方面表现良好,但出现瘀伤和瘀点,血涂片显示孤立性血小板减少症。同样重要的是,我们要排除其他替代原因,并在与血液学团队讨论后立即使用 IVIG 治疗 ITP。此外,密切的血液学随访导致血小板完全恢复并安全恢复常规儿童免疫接种。

title: National and Regional Trends in Childhood Vaccination Coverage in Türkiye, 1985–2025: An Ecological Time Series Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: National averages may conceal regional declines in childhood vaccination. I described trends in administrative coverage published for Türkiye and its regions through 2025. Methods: Coverage of the third diphtheria–pertussis–tetanus dose (DPT3), BCG, third hepatitis B dose (HBV3), first measles-containing dose (MCV1) and pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) was extracted from Ministry of Health publications. Joinpoint regression with Bonferroni adjustment was applied to the 12 NUTS-1 regions for 2002–2025 and repeated for 2009–2025, 2019–2025 and alternative specifications. Results: In 2025, national coverage was 94% for DPT3, 93% for BCG and 92% for MCV1 and the PCV booster. Regional indicators rose steeply until joinpoints in 2006–2012, years that overlap schedule and reporting changes. Later slopes were mostly negative; in the principal models, six DPT3 or MCV1 declines met the adjusted threshold in 2009–2025, all in Central Anatolia, Western Anatolia and the Black Sea regions, and none in the other windows. MCV1 declines in Central Anatolia and Western Black Sea persisted under every specification. BCG declined in the same regions; all PCV booster slopes were negative, none meeting the threshold. Units reporting at least 95% coverage fell from 80 to 32 of 81 for DPT3 and from 75 to 19 for MCV1 during 2013–2025; the 2018 survey DPT3 estimate was 19 points below the administrative value. Conclusions: Published coverage has plateaued and, in central and Black Sea regions, declined slowly, most consistently for MCV1. Its link to true uptake is uncertain. Active recall in these regions, a national coverage survey and a denominator audit are needed.

abstract_zh: 背景/目标:全国平均水平可能掩盖了儿童 疫苗接种 的区域下降。我描述了截至 2025 年土耳其及其地区发布的行政覆盖范围的趋势。方法:白喉-百日咳-破伤风第三剂 (DPT3)、卡介苗、乙型肝炎第三剂 (HBV3)、含 麻疹 的第一剂 (MCV1) 和肺炎球菌结合物 疫苗 (PCV) 的覆盖范围摘自卫生部出版物。结合 Bonferroni 调整的连接点回归应用于 2002-2025 年的 12 个 NUTS-1 区域,并在 2009-2025 年、2019-2025 年和替代规范中重复。结果:到 2025 年,DPT3 的全国覆盖率为 94%,BCG 的全国覆盖率为 93%,MCV1 和 PCV 加强疫苗的全国覆盖率为 92%。区域指标急剧上升,直到 2006 年至 2012 年的连接点,这些年份与时间表和报告变化重叠。后来的斜率大多为负;在主要模型中,2009-2025 年有 6 次 DPT3 或 MCV1 下降达到调整后的阈值,全部位于安纳托利亚中部、安纳托利亚西部和黑海地区,其他窗口中没有一次。在各种规格下,安纳托利亚中部和黑海西部的 MCV1 持续下降。BCG 在同一地区有所下降;所有 PCV 助推器斜率均为负,没有达到阈值。2013 年至 2025 年期间,报告覆盖率至少 95% 的单位从 DPT3 的 81 个单位中的 80 个下降到 32 个,MCV1 的单位从 75 个下降到 19 个;2018 年调查 DPT3 估计值比行政值低 19 个百分点。结论:已发表的报道已趋于稳定,在中部和黑海地区,缓慢下降,MCV1 的报道最为一致。它与真实吸收率的联系尚不确定。这些地区需要积极召回、全国范围调查和分母审计。

title: SAKTI: DEVELOPMENT OF AN INTEGRATED HEALTH ANALYTICS DASHBOARD TO SUPPORT DATA-DRIVEN DECISION-MAKING AT THE SLEMAN DISTRICT HEALTH OFFICE
abstract: Objective: This study aimed to develop a web-based integrated health analytics dashboard prototype named SAKTI, an acronym for Sistem Analitik Kesehatan Terintegrasi (Integrated Health Analytics System), as a decision-support tool at the Sleman District Health Office. Method: The system was developed using the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) approach with the Waterfall model, encompassing requirement analysis, system design, implementation, and initial testing. The initial dataset used in the prototype included three priority health indicators in Sleman Regency for the 2023–2025 period: dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) and measles in the Disease Prevention and Control Department, and stunting in the Public Health Department. Results: This study produced a web-based SAKTI dashboard prototype with a modular architecture designed to represent four main departments at the Sleman District Health Office: Disease Prevention and Control, Public Health, Health Services, and Health Resources. In the initial development stage, active data implementation focused on two modules—Disease Prevention and Control and Public Health—while the Health Services and Health Resources modules were prepared as integration-ready modules. The dashboard features two-factor authentication, trend charts, distribution maps, demographic visualizations, and cross-department summary tables. The resulting visualizations effectively illustrated differences in indicator dynamics, including a rise in dengue hemorrhagic fever cases, a decline in the measles positivity rate, and a decrease in stunting prevalence alongside inter-area disparities. Novelty: SAKTI serves as a proof-of-concept for an integrated health dashboard that provides an initial foundation for strengthening data-driven decision-making at the district health office level.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a web-based integrated health analytics dashboard named SAKTI to support data-driven decision-making at the Sleman District Health Office. The system was developed using the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) approach with the Waterfall model, incorporating requirement analysis, system design, implementation, and initial testing. The initial dataset included three priority health indicators: dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF), measles, and stunting. The prototype dashboard features a modular architecture with four main departments represented, including Disease Prevention and Control, Public Health, Health Services, and Health Resources. It includes functionalities such as two-factor authentication, trend charts, distribution maps, demographic visualizations, and cross-department summary tables. The resulting visualizations demonstrated differences in health indicator dynamics, such as an increase in DHF cases, a decline in measles positivity rate, and a decrease in stunting prevalence. The study highlights SAKTI as a proof-of-concept for an integrated health dashboard that can strengthen data-driven decision-making at the district health office level. The evidence is based on the initial development stage and features of the dashboard, with a moderate confidence level due to the absence of detailed results and limitations.

abstract_zh: 目标:本研究旨在开发一个名为 SAKTI 的基于网络的综合健康分析仪表板原型,SAKTI 是 Sistem Analitik Kesehatan Terintegrasi(综合健康分析系统)的缩写,作为 Sleman 地区卫生办公室的决策支持工具。方法:该系统是使用系统开发生命周期(SDLC)方法和瀑布模型开发的,包括需求分析、系统设计、实施和初始测试。原型中使用的初始数据集包括斯勒曼县 2023-2025 年期间的三个优先健康指标:疾病预防和控制部门的登革出血热 (DHF) 和 麻疹,以及公共卫生部门的发育迟缓。结果:本研究制作了一个基于网络的 SAKTI 仪表板原型,该原型采用模块化架构,旨在代表斯勒曼地区卫生办公室的四个主要部门:疾病预防和控制、公共卫生、卫生服务和卫生资源。在最初的开发阶段,主动数据实施主要集中在疾病预防控制和公共卫生两个模块,而卫生服务和卫生资源模块则准备为集成就绪模块。仪表板具有双因素身份验证、趋势图、分布图、人口统计可视化和跨部门汇总表。由此产生的可视化效果有效地说明了指标动态的差异,包括登革出血热病例的增加、麻疹 阳性率的下降以及发育迟缓的 麻疹 的减少以及区域间差异。新颖性:SAKTI 作为综合健康仪表板的概念验证,为加强地区卫生办公室级别的数据驱动决策奠定了初步基础。

analysis_zh.main_results: 这项研究制作了一个基于网络的 SAKTI 仪表板原型,该原型具有模块化架构,旨在代表斯勒曼地区卫生办公室的四个主要部门:疾病预防和控制、公共卫生、卫生服务和卫生资源。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 仪表板具有双因素身份验证、趋势图、分布图、人口统计可视化和跨部门汇总表。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 由此产生的可视化效果有效地说明了指标动态的差异,包括登革出血热病例的增加、麻疹 阳性率的下降以及发育迟缓的 麻疹 的减少以及区域间差异。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 新颖性:SAKTI 作为综合健康仪表板的概念验证,为加强地区卫生办公室级别的数据驱动决策奠定了初步基础。

title: Sarampión: de la eliminación al rebrote. Revisión de la literatura y recomendaciones actuales
abstract: El sarampión es una enfermedad viral altamente contagiosa, prevenible por vacunación y de notificación obligatoria, que representa un problema de salud pública vigente. Su agente causal es el virus del sarampión (familia Paramyxoviridae), de serotipo único, transmitido por vía aérea con un número reproductivo básico de 12 a 18. La presentación clínica clásica incluye un pródromo de fiebre, tos, coriza y conjuntivitis, seguido de las manchas de Koplik y un exantema maculopapular cefalocaudal. El diagnóstico se confirma mediante serología (IgM específica), reacción en cadena de la polimerasa o cultivo viral. El tratamiento es fundamentalmente de soporte; en pacientes pediátricos, la vitamina A reduce la mortalidad hasta un 62%, por lo que está recomendada por la OMS en este grupo de pacientes. Las complicaciones ocurren en aproximadamente el 30% de los casos; las más frecuentes son diarrea (8%) y otitis media (7-9%), y las complicaciones graves incluyen neumonía, diarrea, encefalitis aguda, encefalomielitis aguda posinfecciosa y, a largo plazo, panencefalitis esclerosante subaguda. Las poblaciones más vulnerables son los menores de 5 años, los adultos jóvenes sin inmunización previa, las embarazadas y los inmunocomprometidos. La vacuna triple vírica (sarampión, rubeola y parotiditis) tiene una eficacia del 97% tras dos dosis y requiere una cobertura poblacional superior al 93% para alcanzar la inmunidad de rebaño. En México, la cobertura vacunal ha disminuido significativamente, lo que derivó en más de 12,000 casos confirmados y más de 33 defunciones durante el brote de 2025-2026, afectando mayoritariamente a niños no vacunados. La profilaxis posexposición con la vacuna triple vírica en un plazo de 72 horas, o con inmunoglobulina en un plazo de 6 días, está indicada para personas susceptibles de alto riesgo. La coordinación mundial, las campañas de vacunación sostenidas y una mayor vigilancia clínica siguen siendo fundamentales para frenar la transmisión.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the ongoing public health problem of measles, emphasizing its high contagiousness and the importance of vaccination. It outlines the clinical presentation, diagnostic methods, and treatment recommendations, particularly highlighting the role of vitamin A in reducing mortality among pediatric patients. The paper also discusses the impact of declining vaccination coverage, as seen in Mexico during the 2025-2026 outbreak, which resulted in over 12,000 confirmed cases and more than 33 deaths. The findings underscore the necessity of sustained vaccination campaigns and clinical vigilance to control transmission. However, the study does not provide detailed statistical analyses or specific outcomes from interventions, which limits the strength of the evidence. The authors conclude that global coordination and improved surveillance remain critical for preventing measles resurgence.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the feasibility of using wastewater sequencing for scalable measles surveillance during outbreaks in South Africa, addressing the need for high-resolution tracking of virus spread and evolution.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed whole-genome amplicon sequencing of wastewater samples from South Africa during the 2024–2025 measles outbreaks, involving multiple provinces and focusing on genotype prevalence and transmission links.
analysis.methods: Wastewater samples were enriched and total nucleic acid extracted using Dynabeads technology, followed by multiplex PCR-based whole-genome sequencing of measles virus.
analysis.main_results: Whole-genome sequencing of wastewater samples revealed shifts in genotype prevalence, detailed transmission links, and previously unreported interprovincial spread of measles virus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interpreted these findings as enabling high-resolution tracking of measles virus spread and evolution, which is novel in using wastewater sequencing for scalable surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for measles, enhancing public health responses to outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges limitations in design, such as the need for further validation and generalizability to other settings, and assesses the evidence strength as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study used wastewater sequencing to track measles virus spread and evolution during outbreaks in South Africa, demonstrating high-resolution surveillance capabilities.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查在南非 麻疹 期间使用废水测序进行可扩展的 麻疹 监测 的可行性,以满足对病毒传播和 进化 进行高分辨率跟踪的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究对2024年至2025年麻疹 暴发期间来自南非的废水样本进行了全基因组扩增子测序,涉及多个省份,重点关注基因型患病率和传播链接。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 Dynabeads 技术对废水样品进行富集并提取总核酸,然后对 麻疹病毒 进行基于多重 PCR 的全 基因组 测序。
elements_zh.main_results: 废水样本的全 基因组 测序揭示了基因型 患病率 的变化、详细的 传播 链接以及之前未报告的 麻疹病毒 的省际传播。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究将这些发现解释为能够对 麻疹病毒 传播和 进化 进行高分辨率跟踪,这在使用废水测序实现可扩展的 监测 方面是新颖的。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为 麻疹 的 监测、诊断 和 治疗 策略提供信息,从而增强对 暴发 的公共卫生应对。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认设计上的局限性,例如需要进一步验证和推广到其他环境,并将证据强度评估为中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查在南非 麻疹 期间使用废水测序进行可扩展的 麻疹 监测 的可行性,以满足对病毒传播和 进化 进行高分辨率跟踪的需求。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究对2024年至2025年麻疹 暴发期间来自南非的废水样本进行了全基因组扩增子测序,涉及多个省份,重点关注基因型患病率和传播链接。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用 Dynabeads 技术对废水样品进行富集并提取总核酸,然后对 麻疹病毒 进行基于多重 PCR 的全 基因组 测序。
analysis_zh.main_results: 废水样本的全 基因组 测序揭示了基因型 患病率 的变化、详细的 传播 链接以及之前未报告的 麻疹病毒 的省际传播。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究将这些发现解释为能够对 麻疹病毒 传播和 进化 进行高分辨率跟踪,这在使用废水测序实现可扩展的 监测 方面是新颖的。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为 麻疹 的 监测、诊断 和 治疗 策略提供信息,从而增强对 暴发 的公共卫生应对。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认设计上的局限性,例如需要进一步验证和推广到其他环境,并将证据强度评估为中等。

full_text: Addressing vaccine hesitancy in pulmonary disease training Until recently, vaccines have been largely regarded as a major triumph of medicine. According to estimates from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), between 1994 and 2023 childhood vaccines prevented roughly 508 million lifetime illnesses, 32 million hospitalizations, and 1,129,000 deaths, and netted $540 billion savings in direct costs and $2.7 trillion in societal costs. Yet vaccine hesitancy, defined by the World Health Organization (WHO) as the delay in acceptance or refusal of vaccines despite availability of vaccination services, is a mounting global phenomenon. It is therefore vital for healthcare providers, and specifically pulmonary disease specialists, to be deliberately trained not just in immunization science and epidemiology, but in the sources of vaccine hesitancy and evidence-based methods to overcome it. Vaccine hesitancy and opposition to vaccine implementation are as old as vaccines themselves, though the sources of concern have shifted over time. For example, early attempts to control smallpox with “inoculation” were met with religious objections, and in later decades, even the medical establishment was dubious of vaccine efficacy due to limited understanding of the role microbes play in disease and the immune system. Today, vaccine hesitancy stems mostly from misinformation and disinformation amplified by social media, which finds fertile soil in an increasingly polarized political climate. This fuels mistrust of healthcare providers and organizations, as noted by a 31.4% reduction of public trust in physicians and hospitals from April 2020 to January 2024, with lower levels of trust associated with refusal of COVID-19 vaccination. This can have far-reaching impacts as demonstrated by the 2025 recrudescence of measles in the United States and Canada attributed to suboptimal vaccination rates. Traditionally, contending with vaccine hesitancy relied on public trust in medical experts. A 1914 address by Sir William Osler to British troops at the outset of World War I serves as a historical example of countering vaccine hesitancy. In his speech “Bacilli and Bullets,” Osler took a pragmatic approach by appealing to reason with epidemiologic and scientific facts, stating, “What I wish to urge is a true knowledge of your foes, not simply of the bullets, but of the much more important enemy—the bacilli.” Osler was alluding to the fact that in the Second Boer War (1899-1902), typhoid was responsible for 64% of the 22,000 British lives lost despite the availability of an effective vaccine developed by Sir Almroth Wright. However, in this present era of undermined trust in expertise and erosion of confidence in established medicine, this approach has not been successful. How, then, are healthcare educators to address vaccine hesitancy? First and foremost, understanding reasons for vaccine hesitancy is paramount. A WHO framework categorizes determinants of vaccine hesitancy into contextual, individual, and group influences, and vaccine-related concerns (Table 1). Specific vaccine myths include the superiority of “natural” immunity, the concept of immune system overload/weakening, vaccine inefficacy, false or overestimated risk of adverse side effects (ie, autistic spectrum disorder), and customizing vaccine schedules to accommodate “too many” vaccines. The World Health Organization’s determinants of vaccine hesitancy. Determinants Examples Contextual influences: Influences arising due to historic, sociocultural, environmental, health system/institutional, economic or political factors Communication and media environmentInfluential leaders, gatekeepers, and anti- or pro-vaccination lobbiesHistorical influencesReligion/culture/gender/socioeconomicPolitics/policiesGeographic barriersPharmaceutical industry Individual and group influences: Influences arising from personal perception of the vaccine or influences of the social/peer environment Experience with past vaccinationBeliefs and attitudes about health and preventionKnowledge/awarenessHealth system and providers—trust and personal experienceRisk/benefit (perceived, heuristic)Immunization as a social norm vs not needed/harmful Vaccination-specific issues: Directly related to vaccine or vaccination Risk/benefit (perceived, heuristic)Immunization as a social norm vs not needed/harmfulRisk/benefit (scientific evidence)Introduction of a new vaccine or new formulationMode of administrationDesign of vaccination program/mode of deliveryReliability and/or source of vaccine supplyVaccination scheduleCostsRole of healthcare professionals Understandably, the pediatric field is leading the effort to reverse the vaccine hesitancy course as vaccines have been recommended for 18 vaccine-preventable diseases between the newborn period and adolescence. Initially, pediatric resident immunization education lacked consistency, as noted in a 2014 survey completed by 92 Association of Pediatric Program Directors members that revealed 59% of the programs lacked formal training on vaccine safety to address parental concerns. The American Academy of Pediatrics is therefore working to reduce vaccine hesitancy by strengthening immunization education for practicing pediatricians and trainees. Data suggest this improves the confidence of healthcare providers to discuss vaccines with parents and patients, which subsequently increases vaccination rates. One pilot study of 45 pediatric residents examining an intervention of an immersive virtual reality curriculum to educate residents on how to address vaccine hesitancy demonstrated a decreased rate of influenza vaccination refusal among patients cared for by residents who received vaccine hesitancy training compared to controls (27.8% vs 37.1%, P = .03). Additionally, the American Board of Pediatrics general pediatrics certification exam consists of 24 domains, with the first domain, Preventive Pediatrics/Well-Child Care, making up 12% of the exam. Specifically in this domain is the topic of immunizations, which includes vaccine hesitancy. In contrast, adult medicine specialties lag. The American Board of Internal Medicine internal medicine and pulmonary disease certification exams have less than 2% of questions directed toward immunization. Data on immunization education specifically for pulmonary trainees are sparse but given the vulnerability to infectious diseases in patients with pulmonary disease, effective immunization dialogue is an essential and life-saving competence for pulmonary disease specialists. In 2022 and 2023, the CDC reported that chronic lower respiratory diseases and COVID-19 were among the top 10 leading causes of death. Recognizing that vaccination in this population is a priority, the Council of Medical Specialty Societies and the CDC are funding the American Thoracic Society (ATS) and 6 other professional societies with the primary aim of increasing vaccination rates in adults. The ATS Vaccine Initiative has partnered with 8 institutions to study strategies to enhance vaccination in adults specifically with respiratory disease and notably is addressing vaccine hesitancy. This is a remarkable opportunity for the ATS and other professional organizations to develop formal immunization science curricula. Structured education will also contribute to pulmonary fellows’ overall clinical competence, with the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education underscoring the mitigation of disease risk factors and communication barriers in patients with complex pulmonary disorders as key milestones. An immunization science program tailored for pulmonary trainees could be modeled after the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society’s Comprehensive Vaccine Education Program and administered via asynchronous online modules with possible clinic-based simulation. An illustrative framework of topics could include: The history and benefits of vaccines. A review of immunology, vaccine mechanisms of action (ie, nucleic acid like messenger RNA), and ingredients (ie, adjuvants). Vaccine development and safety monitoring processes (Figure 1). Biostatistical concepts that determine vaccine efficacy. Vaccine-preventable diseases and the recommended associated vaccines for patients with respiratory disease. Examples include COVID-19, influenza, respiratory syncytial virus, pertussis, pneumococcus, and Haemophilus influenzae type b. Sources of vaccine hesitancy and addressing common misconceptions. Communicating vaccine recommendations: Delivering strong vaccine recommendations to patients using a presumptive format (ie, Instead of asking, “How do you feel about a pneumococcal vaccine today?,” the healthcare provider would state, “You are due to receive the pneumococcal vaccine today.”) Utilizing active listening and motivational interviewing skills for vaccine-hesitant patients such as asking open-ended questions, offering affirmations and support of autonomy, reflecting on prior patient experiences, and sharing of information. Vaccine development and licensing is overseen by the FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research and Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee, with recommendations for use determined by the CDC’s ACIP. Abbreviations: ACIP, Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices; BEST, Biologics Effectiveness and Safety System; BLA, Biologics License Application; CDC, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; CISA, Clinical Immunization Safety Assessment; FDA, US Food and Drug Administration; IND, Investigational New Drug application; R & D, research and development; VAERS, Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System; VSD, Vaccine Safety Datalink. Dr. Osler concluded his 1914 address by appealing to the greater good but acknowledging the individual autonomy that existed in the British army stating, “It [typhoid fever] can be prevented, it must be prevented; but, meanwhile, the decision is in your hands. ...” A robust public health system provides solid footing for a flourishing society. Vaccines are vital to this, but their success ultimately requires a strong, trusting partnership between healthcare providers and the public. As healthcare educators, we need to seize the initiative to ensure our trainees are the vanguard of improvement. title: Undernutrition among children aged 6–59 months attending Afgooye Hospital, Somalia: a facility-based cross-sectional study

source_records.title: Undernutrition among children aged 6–59 months attending Afgooye Hospital, Somalia: a facility-based cross-sectional study

priority_tier_reason: 补充性记录、预印本或证据完整度有限
full_text: AbstractBackgroundChild undernutrition remains a major public-health problem in Somalia, where conflict, climate shocks, displacement and food insecurity strain health and WASH services. National surveys inform planning but do not describe the children who present to individual facilities. We describe anthropometric undernutrition among children aged 6–59 months attending Afgooye Hospital.MethodsIn this facility-based cross-sectional study (February–March 2025), children attending growth monitoring were recruited consecutively. Weight, length/height and mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) were measured following WHO procedures, and Z-scores were calculated with WHO Anthro using the WHO Child Growth Standards. Analysis was descriptive, with Wilson 95% confidence intervals. Displacement status was not recorded and duplicate measurements were not taken.ResultsOf 422 children, 94.3% (95% CI 91.7–96.1) were stunted (55.9% severely) and 79.9% (95% CI 75.8–83.4) were wasted by weight-for-height Z-score, whereas 39.1% (95% CI 34.6–43.8) had acute malnutrition by MUAC. Colostrum was reported for 47.6% of children, prior exclusive breastfeeding for 20.6%, and diarrhoea in the preceding two weeks for 64.5%. These estimates could not be checked against duplicate measurements and should be interpreted cautiously.ConclusionChildren attending Afgooye Hospital in this two-month period had a very high burden of anthropometric undernutrition. Because recruitment was consecutive, at one facility, in the Jilaal dry season, and without duplicate measurements, the estimates describe this clinic cohort and are not district prevalence. They support strengthened facility-based screening and care, and representative, seasonally repeated community surveillance that records displacement status.Keywords: Afgooye, child nutrition, facility-based study, MUAC, Somalia, stunting, undernutrition, wasting 2.Materials and methods2.1.Design and settingWe conducted a facility-based cross-sectional study from February to March 2025 at Afgooye Hospital, about 30 km from Mogadishu, which provides maternal and child health services including growth monitoring. The study characterizes children attending this service; it was not designed to estimate community or district prevalence.2.2.ParticipantsChildren aged 6–59 months attending the hospital for growth monitoring were eligible, and caregivers gave informed consent. Children already enrolled at an earlier visit were excluded to avoid duplicates. The study records do not specify whether children already enrolled in a nutrition programme, referred for acute malnutrition or admitted as inpatients were eligible, or whether bilateral pitting oedema was assessed; these gaps are acknowledged as limitations.2.3.Sample size and recruitmentThe single-proportion formula was used with 95% confidence, 5% absolute precision and an expected prevalence of 50% [which maximizes p(1 − p) when no reliable local estimate exists], giving 384 children; adding 10% for non-response gave a target of 422. The calculation addresses precision of a prevalence estimate, not power for association analyses. Eligible children were recruited consecutively from the clinic attendance register until 422 were enrolled. This non-probability approach may over-represent children whose caregivers sought care because of growth or health concerns, limiting generalizability.2.4.Data collectionTrained data collectors used an interviewer-administered questionnaire covering socio-demographic characteristics, feeding history, recent illness and vaccination, supplemented by review of vaccination cards and medical records. Completed questionnaires were checked daily for completeness and consistency. Food-group questions were not analysed because the questionnaire did not define a reproducible recall period or a validated dietary-diversity score. Displacement status (host community versus internally displaced) was not collected and was not inferred retrospectively; no analysis by displacement status is reported.2.5.Definitions of variablesDefinitions applied in this analysis were as follows; caregiver report was the source unless stated.Vaccination: complete if the card or caregiver report documented all doses due for the child’s age in the Somali EPI schedule (BCG, OPV0, three doses of OPV and pentavalent, pneumococcal conjugate vaccine, and measles-containing vaccine from 9 months); incomplete if at least one but not all due doses were received; none if no dose was documented or reported. Assessment against age-appropriate doses prevented infants under 9 months being classed as incomplete for measles vaccine alone.Colostrum feeding: the first yellowish milk was given rather than discarded. Prior exclusive breastfeeding: only breast milk (apart from oral rehydration salts, vitamins, minerals or prescribed medicines) during the first six months of life; this is a retrospective report for children of all ages and is not equivalent to the survey indicator restricted to infants under six months. Currently breastfeeding: any breast milk at interview.Recent illness (preceding two weeks): diarrhoea was three or more loose or watery stools in 24 h; respiratory-infection symptoms were cough with short, rapid or difficult breathing attributed to a chest problem; fever was caregiver-reported and not measured. History of measles: reported clinical diagnosis at any time or documentation in the record. Deworming: albendazole or mebendazole in the previous six months, by report or record.Caregiver education: no formal education versus any formal schooling. Household income: caregiver-reported total household income in the previous month, in US dollars, categorized as below versus at or above US$100.2.6.Anthropometric measurement and data qualityMeasurements followed WHO procedures. Weight was measured to the nearest 0.1 kg on a Salter scale with the child in light clothing. Recumbent length was measured for children under 24 months and standing height with a mechanical stadiometer from 24 months. MUAC was measured with a tricolour tape Data collectors were trained, equipment was checked, and forms were reviewed daily. The source used to establish each child’s age (birth certificate, health card or caregiver recall) was not documented. Duplicate measurements and formal inter-observer standardization were not carried out.No flagged-value screening, independent re-entry of data or other formal data-quality audit was performed or documented, and Z-score distributions were not retained for this report. Prevalence estimates are therefore reported as recorded and have not been independently verified; the implications are discussed in Section 4.2.2.7.Nutritional statusHeight-for-age (HAZ) and weight-for-height (WHZ) Z-scores were calculated with WHO Anthro and the WHO Child Growth Standards. Stunting was HAZ < −2 SD (severe <−3 SD) and wasting was WHZ < −2 SD (severe <−3 SD). By MUAC, <11.5 cm indicated severe and 11.5 to <12.5 cm moderate acute malnutrition. WHZ- and MUAC-based classifications were compared at the aggregate level only.2.8.Statistical analysisData were analysed in SPSS version 26. We report counts and percentages with Wilson 95% confidence intervals. The study was not designed to identify determinants, and we did not fit regression models for three reasons: (i) only 24 children were not stunted (and 85 not wasted), so models with several covariates would be unstable and prone to sparse-data bias; (ii) the sample size was calculated for prevalence precision rather than for association analyses; and (iii) odds ratios from logistic models overstate prevalence ratios when the outcome is common, and non-random facility selection would make any such estimate hard to interpret. No p-values or adjusted estimates are presented, and statements about associated factors are not made.2.9.Ethical approvalThe Institutional Review Board of SIMAD University, Mogadishu, approved the study. Written and verbal informed consent was obtained from caregivers. Confidentiality and anonymity were maintained. 3.Results3.1.ParticipantsA total of 422 children were analysed. Counts of children screened, ineligible, declining or excluded for incomplete anthropometry were not recorded, so a participant-flow diagram cannot be provided. Most children were aged 6–11 months (38.6%) or 12–23 months (38.2%), and 55.2% were female. Most caregivers were married (69.2%), 46.4% had no formal education, and 70.4% of households reported income below US$100 per month (Table 1).Table 1Socio-demographic, feeding and recent health characteristics of children aged 6–59 months attending Afgooye Hospital, Somalia, February–March 2025 (N = 422).DomainCharacteristicn (%)Socio-demographicAge 6–11 months163 (38.6)Age 12–23 months161 (38.2)Age 24–59 months98 (23.2)Female233 (55.2)Male189 (44.8)Caregiver married292 (69.2)Caregiver widowed, divorced or separated130 (30.8)Caregiver with no formal education196 (46.4)Caregiver with any formal education226 (53.6)Household income <US$100/month297 (70.4)Household income ≥US$100/month125 (29.6)FeedingReceived colostrum201 (47.6)Did not receive colostrum221 (52.4)Previously exclusively breastfed87 (20.6)Not previously exclusively breastfed335 (79.4)Currently breastfeeding148 (35.1)Not currently breastfeeding274 (64.9)VaccinationComplete131 (31.0)Incomplete94 (22.3)None197 (46.7)Recent healthDiarrhoea, preceding two weeks272 (64.5)No diarrhoea150 (35.5)Respiratory-infection symptoms195 (46.2)No respiratory-infection symptoms227 (53.8)Fever, preceding two weeks211 (50.0)No fever211 (50.0)History of measles155 (36.7)No history of measles267 (63.3)Dewormed in previous six months121 (28.7)Not dewormed301 (71.3)Percentages are within each variable (N = 422). Vaccination was complete in 31.0%, incomplete in 22.3% and absent in 46.7% (197/422). In the preceding two weeks, 64.5% (272/422) had diarrhoea, 46.2% had respiratory-infection symptoms and 50.0% had fever; 36.7% had a history of measles and 28.7% had been dewormed in the previous six months (Table 1). All these variables rely on caregiver report and are subject to recall and social-desirability bias.3.3.Nutritional statusStunting affected 94.3% (398/422; 95% CI 91.7–96.1) of children, including 55.9% with severe stunting. Wasting by WHZ affected 79.9% (337/422; 95% CI 75.8–83.4), almost all of it moderate (76.1%; severe 3.8%). By MUAC, 34.1% had moderate and 5.0% severe acute malnutrition, 39.1% (95% CI 34.6–43.8) in total, while 60.9% were normal (Table 2; Figures 1, 2). full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractBackgroundChild undernutrition remains a major public-health problem in Somalia, where conflict, climate shocks, displacement and food insecurity strain health and WASH services. National surveys inform planning but do not describe the children who present to individual facilities. We describe anthropometric undernutrition among children aged 6–59 months attending Afgooye Hospital.MethodsIn this facility-based cross-sectional study (February–March 2025), children attending growth monitoring were recruited consecutively. Weight, length/height and mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) were measured following WHO procedures, and Z-scores were calculated with WHO Anthro using the WHO Child Growth Standards. Analysis was descriptive, with Wilson 95% confidence intervals. Displacement status was not recorded and duplicate measurements were not taken.ResultsOf 422 children, 94.3% (95% CI 91.7–96.1) were stunted (55.9% severely) and 79.9% (95% CI 75.8–83.4) were wasted by weight-for-height Z-score, whereas 39.1% (95% CI 34.6–43.8) had acute malnutrition by MUAC. Colostrum was reported for 47.6% of children, prior exclusive breastfeeding for 20.6%, and diarrhoea in the preceding two weeks for 64.5%. These estimates could not be checked against duplicate measurements and should be interpreted cautiously.ConclusionChildren attending Afgooye Hospital in this two-month period had a very high burden of anthropometric undernutrition. Because recruitment was consecutive, at one facility, in the Jilaal dry season, and without duplicate measurements, the estimates describe this clinic cohort and are not district prevalence. They support strengthened facility-based screening and care, and representative, seasonally repeated community surveillance that records displacement status.Keywords: Afgooye, child nutrition, facility-based study, MUAC, Somalia, stunting, undernutrition, wasting
full_text_sections.methods: 2.Materials and methods2.1.Design and settingWe conducted a facility-based cross-sectional study from February to March 2025 at Afgooye Hospital, about 30 km from Mogadishu, which provides maternal and child health services including growth monitoring. The study characterizes children attending this service; it was not designed to estimate community or district prevalence.2.2.ParticipantsChildren aged 6–59 months attending the hospital for growth monitoring were eligible, and caregivers gave informed consent. Children already enrolled at an earlier visit were excluded to avoid duplicates. The study records do not specify whether children already enrolled in a nutrition programme, referred for acute malnutrition or admitted as inpatients were eligible, or whether bilateral pitting oedema was assessed; these gaps are acknowledged as limitations.2.3.Sample size and recruitmentThe single-proportion formula was used with 95% confidence, 5% absolute precision and an expected prevalence of 50% [which maximizes p(1 − p) when no reliable local estimate exists], giving 384 children; adding 10% for non-response gave a target of 422. The calculation addresses precision of a prevalence estimate, not power for association analyses. Eligible children were recruited consecutively from the clinic attendance register until 422 were enrolled. This non-probability approach may over-represent children whose caregivers sought care because of growth or health concerns, limiting generalizability.2.4.Data collectionTrained data collectors used an interviewer-administered questionnaire covering socio-demographic characteristics, feeding history, recent illness and vaccination, supplemented by review of vaccination cards and medical records. Completed questionnaires were checked daily for completeness and consistency. Food-group questions were not analysed because the questionnaire did not define a reproducible recall period or a validated dietary-diversity score. Displacement status (host community versus internally displaced) was not collected and was not inferred retrospectively; no analysis by displacement status is reported.2.5.Definitions of variablesDefinitions applied in this analysis were as follows; caregiver report was the source unless stated.Vaccination: complete if the card or caregiver report documented all doses due for the child’s age in the Somali EPI schedule (BCG, OPV0, three doses of OPV and pentavalent, pneumococcal conjugate vaccine, and measles-containing vaccine from 9 months); incomplete if at least one but not all due doses were received; none if no dose was documented or reported. Assessment against age-appropriate doses prevented infants under 9 months being classed as incomplete for measles vaccine alone.Colostrum feeding: the first yellowish milk was given rather than discarded. Prior exclusive breastfeeding: only breast milk (apart from oral rehydration salts, vitamins, minerals or prescribed medicines) during the first six months of life; this is a retrospective report for children of all ages and is not equivalent to the survey indicator restricted to infants under six months. Currently breastfeeding: any breast milk at interview.Recent illness (preceding two weeks): diarrhoea was three or more loose or watery stools in 24 h; respiratory-infection symptoms were cough with short, rapid or difficult breathing attributed to a chest problem; fever was caregiver-reported and not measured. History of measles: reported clinical diagnosis at any time or documentation in the record. Deworming: albendazole or mebendazole in the previous six months, by report or record.Caregiver education: no formal education versus any formal schooling. Household income: caregiver-reported total household income in the previous month, in US dollars, categorized as below versus at or above US$100.2.6.Anthropometric measurement and data qualityMeasurements followed WHO procedures. Weight was measured to the nearest 0.1 kg on a Salter scale with the child in light clothing. Recumbent length was measured for children under 24 months and standing height with a mechanical stadiometer from 24 months. MUAC was measured with a tricolour tape Data collectors were trained, equipment was checked, and forms were reviewed daily. The source used to establish each child’s age (birth certificate, health card or caregiver recall) was not documented. Duplicate measurements and formal inter-observer standardization were not carried out.No flagged-value screening, independent re-entry of data or other formal data-quality audit was performed or documented, and Z-score distributions were not retained for this report. Prevalence estimates are therefore reported as recorded and have not been independently verified; the implications are discussed in Section 4.2.2.7.Nutritional statusHeight-for-age (HAZ) and weight-for-height (WHZ) Z-scores were calculated with WHO Anthro and the WHO Child Growth Standards. Stunting was HAZ < −2 SD (severe <−3 SD) and wasting was WHZ < −2 SD (severe <−3 SD). By MUAC, <11.5 cm indicated severe and 11.5 to <12.5 cm moderate acute malnutrition. WHZ- and MUAC-based classifications were compared at the aggregate level only.2.8.Statistical analysisData were analysed in SPSS version 26. We report counts and percentages with Wilson 95% confidence intervals. The study was not designed to identify determinants, and we did not fit regression models for three reasons: (i) only 24 children were not stunted (and 85 not wasted), so models with several covariates would be unstable and prone to sparse-data bias; (ii) the sample size was calculated for prevalence precision rather than for association analyses; and (iii) odds ratios from logistic models overstate prevalence ratios when the outcome is common, and non-random facility selection would make any such estimate hard to interpret. No p-values or adjusted estimates are presented, and statements about associated factors are not made.2.9.Ethical approvalThe Institutional Review Board of SIMAD University, Mogadishu, approved the study. Written and verbal informed consent was obtained from caregivers. Confidentiality and anonymity were maintained.
